display.text:
21/05/2019

Dr Mary Bellamy
Plastic Surgery Consultant
Shepton Hospital
Shepton

Dear Dr Bellamy,
Re: Mr Richard McKie, aged 32 years

Thank you for seeing Mr McKie, who requires plastic or maxillofacial surgery due to a right
blowout fracture following a motorcycle accident.

Today, Mr McKie was admitted to our Emergency Department after a high-velocity
motorcycle accident trauma. He was vitally unstable with respiratory distress, but his
Glasgow coma scale was intact. He had a cervical collar in situ and his pulse-oximetry was
88% on room air. His thorax examination revealed right distant breath sounds along with
hyper-resonance which indicates right tension pneumothorax. Therefore, a prompt needle
decompression was conducted after which a right chest tube had was inserted. In terms of
medication, he was given ampicillin-sulbactam, hydromorphone, omeprazole and
enoxaparin.

Regarding Mr McKie’s secondary survey, he had right periorbital ecchymosis with edema,
decreased visual acuity, mild enophthalmos and right hyperalgesia in the distribution of the
infraorbital nerve. He also had diplopia especially in upgaze which may indicate a blowout
fracture. A Head CT confirmed the blowout fracture with inferior rectus entrapment and a
Lefort type two fracture. Now he is vitally and hemodynamically stable and will remain in
overnight after which he will be transferred into your department.

It would be greatly appreciated valued if you could manage Mr McKie’s condition and keep
me updated on the outcome. If you require any further clarification, please do not hesitate
to contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
